title: Computer Science
summary: A rigorous three-year independent-study pathway spanning mathematical foundations, programming, algorithms, systems, data, networks, software engineering, security, AI, human-centered computing, ethics, research, a coherent concentration, and a two-stage defended capstone.
notice: Course Atlas is not a university or accreditor. It awards no degree, diploma, academic credit, transfer credit, professional license, or guaranteed provider certificate. Completion evidence is a self-directed portfolio that another person may evaluate independently.
workload: Every course carries 4 Course Atlas credits and 160 nominal hours: eight ordered topic blocks containing sixteen exact weekly assignments of 10 hours each. The 30-course pathway remains approximately 4,800 hours across six recommended 20-week terms, including assessment windows and breaks.
outcomes: Build reliable software from requirements through design, implementation, testing, review, deployment, and maintenance.
Apply mathematical, algorithmic, statistical, and theoretical reasoning to computing problems.
Explain and evaluate computer architecture, operating systems, networks, databases, distributed systems, and security.
Develop data-driven and intelligent systems with reproducible evaluation and explicit limitations.
Research human needs, design accessible interactions, and analyze computing's ethical and social consequences.
Plan, build, evaluate, document, and publicly defend a substantial capstone artifact.

courses.title: Computer Architecture: From Logic to Machine
courses.summary: Digital logic, instruction sets, datapath and control, pipelining, memory hierarchy, virtual memory, I/O, parallelism, and measured performance.
courses.first: Design an ALU slice from Boolean equations and minimize two outputs with Karnaugh maps. Keep Equations, minimized forms, schematic, exhaustive truth-table simulation.
outcomes: Design, analyze, and defend a processor and memory hierarchy using functional tests, hazard analysis, and measured performance evidence.
Produce independently checkable evidence of practice and correct weaknesses after assessment.
State assumptions, tradeoffs, safety or ethical limits, and unanswered questions.

Record tool versions, cite every reused source or code fragment, preserve raw inputs, and do not publish provider answer keys.

rubric.description: Research ethics and quality in CS440 Evidence-to-Prototype Design Review is scored from “De-identified research and task-analysis packet” while the learner must turn consented inquiry evidence into task models, requirements, three divergent designs, and a low-fidelity prototype. Award 25 points when scope, affected parties, abuse or failure cases, mitigations, negative tests, and residual limits are evidenced explicitly; award 15 when the primary safeguard works, but one affected group, misuse case, negative test, or residual risk is omitted; award 0 when the work exceeds its authorized scope, hides a material harm, or provides no evidence that the safeguard works.

Evidence synthesis in CS440 Evidence-to-Prototype Design Review is scored from “Alternative sketches, decision matrix, and prototype” while the learner must turn consented inquiry evidence into task models, requirements, three divergent designs, and a low-fidelity prototype. courses.title: Parallel Computing
courses.summary: DAG and work-span cost models, work-efficient parallel algorithms, scheduling, shared and distributed memory, locality, profiling, and scaling.
courses.first: Draw computation DAGs for reduce, map, divide-and-conquer, and nested loops. Keep Four DAGs, work/span recurrences, parallelism values, and critical paths.
outcomes: Design, implement, analyze, and defend a work-efficient parallel program using theoretical bounds and reproducible performance evidence.
Produce independently checkable evidence of practice and correct weaknesses after assessment.
State assumptions, tradeoffs, safety or ethical limits, and unanswered questions.
setup: Open and bookmark CMU 15-210 — Course Book — Chapter 1: Introduction; work and span — https://www.cs.cmu.edu/afs/cs/academic/class/15210-f13/www/lectures/book.pdf.
Create a version-controlled workspace with weekly work, tests, assessment submissions, rubrics, corrections, and evidence in separate folders.
Record tool versions, cite every reused source or code fragment, preserve raw inputs, and do not publish provider answer keys.
